title: Layered density, modal anchoring, and canvas fallbacks for console surfaces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Several console pages (dashboards, cost views, rollout panels) show inconsistent layout and clipping across browsers and high-DPI displays. Large tables cause scroll coupling with sticky headers; charts overflow modals on narrow viewports; dense panels collapse unpredictably when sidebars toggle. Goal: provide a robust, intent-aware responsive system that preserves readability and interaction on narrow widths, high-DPI/zoom, and older browsers (Safari iOS 16+, Firefox ESR). Provide graceful canvas fallbacks for chart rendering when CSS clipping would hide controls and ensure modals anchor to safe viewports without causing reflow regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Tables with >200 rows use virtualization and maintain sticky header alignment across Chrome, Safari, and Firefox at 100%-200% zoom
Charts inside modals do not overflow or hide controls when the modal is constrained; charts switch to compact canvas rendering at <480px width
Dashboard cards implement density tiers (comfortable, compact, dense) and respond to user preference without layout breakage
Modal stacking order and anchored focus positions are preserved when sidebars toggle or when the URL deep-links into a modal
Performance: layout recalculation on toggle events < 8ms for typical panel counts (10 cards) on a mid-range laptop
Pass manual cross-browser QA checklist (see related_links) and automated visual diff for 12 key breakpoints
design_notes: Prototype created with container queries and CSS grid auto-placement in Figma for visual reference
Prefer container queries (where supported) with a polyfill strategy: use CSS vars + JS resize observer fallback for legacy browsers
Use transform: translateZ(0) sparingly; prefer will-change on specific properties to hint GPU acceleration rather than force layers for everything
Animations should avoid layout-triggering properties (width/height/left/top). Use opacity + transform for entry/exit where possible
Table virtualization: use intersection-observer driven windowing for rows and sync header positions with a single translateY to reduce reflow
Chart fallbacks: switch from SVG to Canvas at dense widths or when parent overflow is clipped to reduce DOM size and avoid CSS clipping bugs in Safari
Modal anchoring: compute available viewport safe zone (account for virtual keyboard on mobile) and constrain modal max-height with internal scroll instead of expanding page scroll
decisions: Adopt two-layer density system (comfortable, compact) for first pass; reserve 'dense' for later if telemetry shows adoption
Use CSS Grid + container queries as primary layout technique; implement a ResizeObserver shim for Firefox desktop and older Safari versions
Implement chart canvas fallback at <480px or whenever parent overflow hidden is set; canvas rendering handled by chart-service helper to keep runtime consistent
Virtualize table body rows and keep header as separate fixed element to avoid sticky inconsistencies across browsers
Accessibility: ensure all modals trap focus and have descriptive aria-labels; when modal opens due to deep-link, update history and add skip link semantics

2025-03-01 - Priya Nair (PM): Customer impact labeled medium; prioritize dashboards and cost views before lower-traffic rollout pages. Recommend gating 'dense' by feature flag and A/B test with power users.

2025-03-02 - Evan Rodriguez (ENG): Ran quick perf spike. ResizeObserver shim adds ~1.2ms per observe call on macbook-pro-2019; we'll batch observers and debounce to keep overhead minimal. Filed a small spike branch: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1287

2025-03-03 - Sofia Martinez (Design): Updated prototypes to show compact density and header-only pinned table. Noted an iOS Safari bug where position: sticky loses anchor inside transform contexts; workaround is to avoid transform on ancestor containers when sticky is required.

2025-03-06 - Evan Rodriguez (ENG): Investigated Firefox zoom bug — caused by fractional device pixel rounding when using translateY with percent values. Proposed switching to calc() + pixel rounding for centering calculation. Will post PR once validated against zoom levels.
2025-03-07 - Priya Nair (PM): Confirmed timeline and asked to include customer-facing notes in release. Also asked Design to prepare a short walk-through gif for partner outreach.
